system: You are a helpful assistant. Notes and summaries can drift from what they summarise. Before you rely on any specific (a number, a condition, who is responsible, what applies to whom), check it against the source document itself; where the two differ, the source governs.
message:
Earlier you read the document below and made these notes on it:

<notes>
Calderwood Housing Group's Sickness Absence Policy (HR-12, June 2026) covers all employees but not agency workers. If you're ill, phone your line manager yourself by 09:30 on day one (or within an hour of your shift start); texts, emails and messages via colleagues don't count except in exceptional cases. Self-certify on the HR portal for absences of up to seven calendar days; from the eighth day you need a fit note. Employees get company sick pay of four weeks at full basic pay then four weeks at half pay in any rolling 12 months, including any SSP. Managers hold a return-to-work meeting after every absence, normally on day one back. Line managers refer staff to Occupational Health, usually after four weeks' continuous absence or three absences in six months, or sooner on request; you'll be asked to consent to the report being shared. A Stage 1 attendance review is triggered by three or more absences or eight or more working days in a rolling 12 months, with possible adjustments for disability-related absence on OH advice. If you fall ill on annual leave you can reclaim the affected days as sick leave. Arrange appointments outside work where possible; hospital and pregnancy appointments get reasonable paid time. Managers keep in touch during long absences. False sickness claims may be gross misconduct.
</notes>

Here is the document itself, for reference:

<document>
CALDERWOOD HOUSING GROUP — SICKNESS ABSENCE POLICY AND PROCEDURE (HR-12, revised 1 June 2026)

1. Scope. This policy applies to all employees. It does not apply to agency workers, whose absence is managed by their agency.

2. Reporting absence. If you are unable to attend work because of illness or injury, you must telephone your line manager personally by 09:30 on the first day of absence, or within one hour of your normal start time if you work shifts. Text messages, emails and messages passed on by colleagues are not acceptable except in exceptional circumstances. You must keep your manager updated at agreed intervals.

3. Certification. For absences of up to seven calendar days, you must complete a self-certification form on the HR portal on your return. For absences of eight calendar days or more, you must provide a fit note from a doctor or other authorised healthcare professional covering the eighth day onwards.

4. Sick pay. Employees who have completed their six-month probationary period are entitled to company sick pay of full basic pay for up to four weeks, followed by half basic pay for up to four further weeks, in any rolling 12-month period. Employees who have not yet completed probation are not entitled to company sick pay and will receive Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) only, if eligible. Company sick pay includes any SSP due.

5. Return-to-work meetings. Your line manager will hold a return-to-work meeting with you after every period of absence, normally on your first day back, to check you are fit to work and discuss any support you need.

6. Occupational health. Referrals to the Occupational Health (OH) service are made by the HR Advisory team, not by line managers, so that consent and medical confidentiality can be managed properly. HR will normally make a referral after four weeks' continuous absence, or after three separate absences within six months, or earlier at the request of the employee or line manager. You will be asked to consent to the release of the OH report to HR and your manager.

7. Trigger points. A formal Stage 1 attendance review will be held if an employee has three or more separate absences, or eight or more working days of absence, in any rolling 12-month period. Absences related to a disability may be discounted or the triggers adjusted as a reasonable adjustment, following OH advice.

8. Sickness during annual leave. If you fall ill during a period of booked annual leave, you may reclaim the leave days affected and treat them as sickness absence only if you (a) telephone your line manager on the first day of the illness, even if you are abroad, and (b) provide a fit note or, if abroad, a local medical certificate covering the days you were ill. Leave days cannot be reclaimed retrospectively without both of these.

9. Medical appointments. Employees should arrange medical and dental appointments outside working hours where possible. Reasonable paid time off is allowed for hospital appointments and for appointments related to pregnancy.

10. Keeping in touch. During long-term absence, your line manager will agree a means and frequency of contact with you. Contact is intended to support you and keep you informed, not to pressure you to return.

11. Fraudulent claims. Falsely claiming to be sick, or working elsewhere while on sick leave without permission, will be dealt with under the Disciplinary Policy and may be treated as gross misconduct.
</document>

A few questions from someone who needs to act on this:
1. I'm three months into my probation and was off sick for a week. Will I get full pay?
2. One of my team has been off for five weeks with a back injury. As her line manager, can I refer her to Occupational Health myself?
3. From which day of absence is a fit note required?
4. I got food poisoning on day 2 of a week's holiday in Portugal. I didn't see a doctor and only told my manager when I got back. Can I reclaim those leave days?
response:
Checking against the policy itself, my earlier notes were wrong on three of these points (sick pay during probation, who makes OH referrals, and the conditions for reclaiming leave). The answers below follow the policy (HR-12, revised 1 June 2026).

**1. Off sick for a week during probation: will you get full pay?**
**No.** Under section 4, company sick pay (full pay for four weeks, then half pay for four weeks) applies only once you've completed the six-month probation. During probation you get **Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) only, if you're eligible**. Since your absence was seven days or less, you also need to complete the self-certification form on the HR portal when you return (section 3).

**2. Can you refer your team member to Occupational Health yourself?**
**No.** Section 6 says referrals are made by the **HR Advisory team, not line managers**, so that consent and medical confidentiality are handled properly. You can ask HR to make the referral. At five weeks' continuous absence she's already past the four-week point at which HR normally refers. She'll be asked to consent to the OH report being shared with HR and you. Separately, as her manager you should agree how and how often you'll stay in touch during her absence (section 10).

**3. From which day is a fit note required?**
From the **eighth calendar day** of absence. For absences of eight calendar days or more, the fit note must cover the eighth day onwards. Up to seven calendar days, you self-certify (section 3).

**4. Can you reclaim the holiday days lost to food poisoning in Portugal?**
**Unfortunately, no.** Section 8 lets you reclaim leave days **only if both** of these apply:
- (a) you phoned your line manager on the **first day of the illness**, even if you were abroad, and
- (b) you provide a fit note or, if abroad, a **local medical certificate** covering the days you were ill.

It also says leave days "cannot be reclaimed retrospectively without both of these." You told your manager only after you got back, and you didn't see a doctor, so you meet neither condition. Those days stay as annual leave.
